figmaExecutionNotes: Use a dark theme foundation with a deep navy hero and lighter content sections for contrast.
Keep hero, trust, gallery, and features all present in the desktop frame; do not stop at hero only.
Do not add form, pricing, testimonials, news, or Why Techjockey because the input does not support them.
Build the trust area as a logo-dominant strip; this is the primary trust signal.
Gallery is mandatory from context and should show relevant AI-generated visual examples for both image and video generation.
For mobile, stack sections in the same order: hero, trust logos, gallery, Seedream features, Seedance features.
Use a single responsive feature-card family for both feature sections to maintain system consistency.
Avoid decorative emptiness in the hero; use purposeful product media or generative compositions on the right side.

heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock the power of next-generation generative AI with Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro for professional visual content creation.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use a premium editorial hero with the background image treated as a full-bleed cinematic canvas, then place a semi-transparent dark gradient overlay to preserve readability. Build the hero as an unexpected asymmetrical composition: left side holds the headline, subheadline, and brand-accent CTA; right side uses a layered gallery stack with one dominant preview card and two smaller offset tiles to communicate both image and video outputs. Add subtle precision-line grid overlays and soft orange glow orbs for depth. Keep the CTA in Techjockey orange, never blue. Use large typography with a dramatic hierarchy, ensuring the H1 is well above 60px and the section feels enterprise-premium, not playful. The visual treatment should signal creative control, quality, and confidence for professional buyers.

repetitionBreakers: Start with a split-visual hero to establish premium control and immediate product continuity.
Follow with a dominant logo proof strip on a dark band to front-load trust.
Use an alternating product rhythm: image-led spotlight first, then a more technical split-panel video section.
Insert a gallery-style showcase to visually break up the long-form content and avoid generic SaaS cards.
End with a high-contrast centered lead form card instead of repeating another feature grid.
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro | AI Images & Video Generation
blueprint.metaDescription: Generate high-quality AI images and videos with ByteDance models Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro. Built for creative teams needing premium visual output, multimodal editing, and cinematic video generation.

sections.backgroundTreatment: dark-gradient with orange accent glow and subtle precision-line overlays
sections.designNote: Hero must answer what this is, who it is for, and what to do next. Keep the left side content-first with a direct headline: AI image and video generation for creative teams and businesses. Use the right side as a premium layered visual gallery of outputs, prompt-to-result panels, and cinematic frames to make the product feel dynamic above the fold. Primary CTA button text must be exactly 'Get started' in accent orange at full opacity.

Place trust immediately after the hero using 3-6 recognisable customer logos in a clean static grid. Since the provided data does not include logos, convert this into a restrained proof band that can hold enterprise brand marks if available; otherwise keep the strip visually reserved and ready for logo insertion. No marquee motion. This section should feel like a credibility reset before the product explanation.

featurePresentation.primaryFeatureTitle: How it works in under 60 seconds

sections.designNote: Replace a generic feature block with a 3-step process section because the warm-traffic sequence demands quick clarity. Present: 1) enter a text prompt or input asset, 2) choose image or video generation mode, 3) refine and download/share. Use a split-panel rhythm with one side showing steps and the other showing a live-like preview of outputs. Keep this section fast, simple, and confidence-building.

featurePresentation.primaryFeatureTitle: Why creative teams trust the output

sections.designNote: Make this an industry-proof section, not a generic testimonial block. Use a strong spotlight panel with 3-4 short proof points tied to visual quality, speed, typographic rendering, identity preservation, and synchronized audio-visual generation. If logos are available, retain them as the main proof signal; if not, reinforce with a metrics-style confidence layer. This section should feel editorial and premium, with a darker background to contrast the prior white process section.

This is the main product deep-dive and should not look like a flat card grid. Use tabs with a preview panel for Seedream 4.5, since it has five features and benefits from controlled comparison. Lead with the strongest click-driving features: high-resolution output, typographic rendering, and multi-image composition with identity preservation. Then introduce Seedance 1.5 Pro as a secondary alternating panel with a more cinematic feel, emphasizing text-to-video, audio-visual sync, multilingual lip-sync, and fast inference. Keep adjacent product blocks visually different from each other.

Add a dedicated visual showcase to break the long page rhythm and demonstrate output quality. Use 6-8 curated tiles: poster-grade image, ad creative, product mockup, storyboard frame, cinematic still, and synchronized video preview. This section should be highly expressive and more visual than textual. Use a masonry-like editorial arrangement rather than uniform cards.

With 5 testimonials, use a 3-card grid and a supporting quote rail rather than a slider. Feature creative roles prominently: Creative Director, Video Producer, Art Director, Marketing Manager, and Creative Lead. Keep the cards concise and specific, emphasizing quality, turnaround time, multimodal editing, and storytelling. This section should feel credible but lighter than the proof band.

Use a clear two-column comparison, not a generic plan grid. One card for Seedream 4.5 and one for Seedance 1.5 Pro, with the video plan visually emphasized because it includes pricing. Keep the copy concise and benefit-oriented. CTA button text must remain exactly 'Get started' for both plans, in solid accent orange. Avoid gray or outlined buttons.

Final conversion section should be a high-contrast floating card on the dark background. Keep it simple, premium, and direct. No multi-step friction. Use a strong headline focused on seeing the tools in action, with a single primary button labeled exactly 'Get started' in full-width on mobile. This should feel like the decisive next step rather than a generic signup endpoint.

blueprint.designPersonality: Premium editorial AI showcase for enterprise creative teams: dark, high-contrast, trust-led, and visually intelligent, with strong logo proof, curated gallery presentation, and refined motion-ready surfaces.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use a premium gallery-led visual system: layered AI output frames, cinematic video stills, prompt-to-output comparison panels, and floating chips for Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro capabilities. Add a logo proof strip immediately under the hero as the dominant trust signal. Include a dedicated gallery section with 6–8 curated output tiles showing poster-grade imagery, product mockups, motion frames, and synchronized audio-visual previews. Use dark background with bright orange highlights, subtle grids, and soft shadows. Keep visuals enterprise-polished rather than playful.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Not enough evidence of a split-media hero; the reference shows a full-width hero band with a left-aligned brand/logo block, large headline, supporting copy, and a compact benefits list beneath. Primary message is stacked vertically rather than paired with a prominent visual panel.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Single-column landing page flow with a strong hero followed by a lead-capture/form block; additional product content appears to be organized as stacked content sections rather than a highly modular dashboard-style layout. Rhythm favors straightforward vertical progression and progressive disclosure.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Lead form appears as a contained card panel with clear boundary and internal field grouping. No evidence of glassmorphism; styling should be read as standard solid-surface card with practical business-lead framing.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary CTA should be visually dominant and action-oriented in the hero and repeated at section level where relevant. Secondary CTA is either absent or de-emphasized. Form submit acts as the primary conversion endpoint rather than multiple competing CTAs.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No pricing pattern evident in the reference; omit pricing from the reusable map or treat as not present.
referenceMap.footerMode: Footer is not visible in the provided reference; default to a minimal utility footer if needed, but there is no evidence of a rich content footer pattern.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Media usage is minimal in the visible reference, with logo imagery in the hero and a form-centric layout. No strong evidence of large illustrative media, video embeds, or media galleries.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Best interpreted as stacked informational sections with headline, brief description, and bullet-like feature rows. Use progressive disclosure: introduce the section with a clear headline and summary, then reveal feature details in short, scannable items.
referenceMap.formPattern: Lead-gen form card placed directly under the hero, with hidden tracking fields, compact field stack, and a conversion-focused headline. Form should be visually separated from marketing copy and optimized for quick submission.
referenceMap.animationStyle: No explicit animation pattern is evidenced in the provided markup; treat motion as minimal or absent, with any animation limited to basic standard UI transitions.
designNotes: Prioritize concise hierarchy: brand, promise, benefits, form.
Favor clear boundaries and practical layouts over decorative treatments.
Use compact bullet lists for value framing.
Keep interactions simple; no evidence for advanced navigation patterns like tabs or accordions.

avoidPatterns: Do not omit the form or conversion pathway
Do not make the hero media-heavy on the right if it competes with the lead-capture path
Do not leave empty black space in the hero or between sections
Do not use unrelated visuals; keep media strictly aligned to AI image and AI video generation
Do not bury trust; logos must be the dominant proof signal
Do not use a light or soft consumer-style aesthetic; keep it enterprise-grade and dark
Do not load only the hero section; the full page should be scrollable with complete content structure
Do not make the sticky top strip non-persistent
designStrategy.reasoning: This page is for solution-aware business buyers evaluating advanced AI image and video generation, so the best strategy is a product-led demo-booking flow with strong logo-first trust. The offer is technical but commercially packaged, which calls for a dark, futuristic, enterprise-oriented layout that immediately communicates capability, then progressively proves value through product sections, gallery examples, pricing/quote cards, and testimonials. Because the visitor trusts logos most, logo proof should be the first credibility layer, with the CTA repeated prominently throughout. A split hero is recommended so the page can combine strong messaging with a compact proof/conversion area without sacrificing clarity or scroll depth.
